request.spec:
Each sheet has a "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. It starts as the real
date. Every decision in the app that depends on the date, and every default date, uses the
sheet's today and never the real clock.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each sheet has a "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. It starts as the real
date. Every decision in the app that depends on the date, and every default date, uses the
sheet's today and never the real clock.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each sheet now has a "today" date that is stored with the sheet, shown on the screen and can be changed there. `bin/e2e` passes: the test sets today to 2026-03-10 and then to 2024-02-29, and after each reload the sheet shows the new date. The test never sends a bad date, and I didn't check that case separately. That means the 400 response for an invalid date and the error shown for it (`sheet-error`) have never been run.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V2__sheet_today.sql`, adds a required `today` column to the `sheet` table. A new sheet gets the real date when it is first loaded, and sheets that already exist are filled with the current date.

**Server:**
- `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}` returns the sheet's id and today.
- `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/today` with `{ "today": "yyyy-MM-dd" }` checks the date first, then loads the sheet and saves it. A badly formed date gets a 400 and a sheet that was never loaded gets a 404; both have their own error handlers.
- `SheetRepository.today(id)` gives server code one place to read the sheet's date instead of the clock.

**Front end:**
- `features/sheet/today.slot.tsx` shows the date (`sheet-today`), with a date input (`sheet-today-input`), a save button (`sheet-today-save`) and an error element (`sheet-error`). A blank or malformed date, or a failed save, shows the error and changes nothing. A successful save updates the shown date and re-reads everything else cached for that sheet.
- `features/sheet/sheet.ts` has `useSheetToday(sheetId)` for front-end code that needs the date.

Nothing else in the app uses dates yet, so nothing had to be moved off the real clock. Anything date-related added later should get its date from `SheetRepository.today()` on the server or `useSheetToday()` on the front end, never from the clock. I didn't add an audit record for changing today, because neither the request nor the test specifies one.
